title: Eventual geometric fibre dimension bound for finitely presented algebraic spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finitely presented if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact), and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and let $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ of an algebraic space to $T_{i_0}$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $f_i:X_i\to T_i$, and put $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $f:X\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix an integer $d\ge0$. A geometric fibre here means the algebraic-space fibre product with $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ along a geometric point, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, using the convention of [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; its dimension is its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Empty fibres impose no condition. If every geometric fibre of $f$ has dimension at most $d$, there is $i\ge i_0$ such that every geometric fibre of $f_j$ has dimension at most $d$ for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 0D4K (lemma-eventually-relative-dimension), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space over an affine base; geometric fibre interpretation and persistence: spaces-morphisms.tex, Tags 06LR (definition-relative-dimension) and 04NS (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change).

proof.text: The quasi-compactness of $f_{i_0}$, tested against the affine scheme $T_{i_0}$, says that $X_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact: use the scheme-test definition in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Thus there is a representable surjective etale map $C\to X_{i_0}$ with $C$ a quasi-compact scheme. Apply [lem-a1-qc-map-affine-etale-neighbourhood] to this map. It gives an affine scheme $U_{i_0}$ and a representable etale map $p_{i_0}:U_{i_0}\to X_{i_0}$ for which $C\times_{X_{i_0}}U_{i_0}\to C$ is surjective. Hence $p_{i_0}$ is surjective: every point of $X_{i_0}$ lifts to $C$ and then to this fibre product, and projecting gives a lift to $U_{i_0}$. This supplies the affine atlas chosen in the source, with $V_{i_0}=T_{i_0}$.

source.place: Tag 0D4K (lemma-eventually-relative-dimension), choice of affine U_0 and V_0; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), realized here using existing atlas nodes

proof.text: Put $g_{i_0}=f_{i_0}\circ p_{i_0}:U_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$. It is locally of finite presentation by the hypothesis that $f_{i_0}$ is locally of finite presentation on compatible etale scheme charts (use the identity chart of $T_{i_0}$). Every algebra $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ is generated over $R$ by the images of $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, so the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] makes $g_{i_0}$ locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since its source and target are affine, it is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], applied to the one-open cover of its target. It is therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Thus $g_{i_0}$ is of finite type, as required for the scheme limit lemma.

source.place: Tag 0D4K, last paragraph: U_0 -> V_0 is locally of finite type; finite type follows because both are affine

proof.text: For $i\ge i_0$ define $U_i=U_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$ and put $U=U_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. The algebraic-space fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $U_i$ with $U_{i_0}\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$, and similarly for $U$. Its etale-cover clause makes the atlas projections $p_i:U_i\to X_i$ and $p:U\to X$ surjective etale. Each $g_i:U_i\to T_i$ and $g:U\to T$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2). The limit $T$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. All $U_i$ and $U$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. They form the limit diagram $g=\varprojlim g_i$: by [def-pc-fibre-product], compatible maps from any scheme $Z$ to all $U_i$ are exactly a map $Z\to U_{i_0}$ and a compatible cone $Z\to T_i$ agreeing at $i_0$, hence exactly a map $Z\to U$. This also proves that $U_j\to U_i\times_{T_i}T_j$ is an isomorphism. Finally all $f_i$ and $f$ are locally of finite type on these charts. Write $X_0=X_{i_0}$, $T_0=T_{i_0}$ and $\Delta_0:X_0\to X_0\times_{T_0}X_0$. For any affine scheme test $Z\to X_i\times_{T_i}X_i$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $Z\times_{X_i\times_{T_i}X_i}X_i$ with $Z\times_{X_0\times_{T_0}X_0}X_0$. The latter is quasi-compact because $\Delta_0$ is quasi-compact. This proves $f_i$ quasi-separated; the same calculation with $T$ proves it for $f$. The tail $i\ge i_0$ is nonempty, directed and cofinal. Explicitly, a cone over this tail extends to any $T_k$ by choosing $j\ge k,i_0$ and composing its map to $T_j$ with $T_j\to T_k$; two choices agree after passing to a common upper bound. Thus its limit is still $T$. Each $T_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since it is affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) applied to its structure map to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and [pqf-lem-affine-local-target].

source.place: Tag 0D4K, base-changed diagrams, affineness, and identification of their limits; cartesian identities written out

proof.text: For $t\in T$ choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the pullback $U_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ of $p$ is still surjective etale. The diagonal test calculation in step 3, now with $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ as base, shows that $X_\Omega$ is quasi-separated over $\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-atlas-dimension] with $k=\Omega$, $Y=X_\Omega$ and atlas $U_\Omega$: it gives $\dim|X_\Omega|=\dim|U_\Omega|$. The affine scheme fibre $U_t$ is of finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], so its coordinate algebra is of finite type by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. Writing $U_t=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the affine fibre-product formula gives $U_\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\Omega)$; swapping tensor factors by $b\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes b$ identifies this with the algebra in 00P3. By the fibre-product identity $U_\Omega=U_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension], $\dim U_t=\dim U_\Omega=\dim|X_\Omega|\le d$. Thus every ordinary fibre of $g$ satisfies the bound. This is an application of the cited dimension equalities, not an identification of ordinary and geometric fibres themselves.

source.place: Tag 0D4K, chart comparison, using decent-spaces.tex Tag 0A4J (lemma-dimension-decent-space), spaces-properties.tex Tag 0A4H (lemma-dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale) and algebra.tex Tag 00P3 (lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-limit-fibre-dimension-bound] to $g_i:U_i\to T_i$ over the tail $i\ge i_0$. Its affine-transition, quasi-compact and quasi-separated base hypotheses and finite-type source maps were checked in step 3. The comparison $U_j\to U_i\times_{T_i}T_j$ is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion: its scheme-test image is the whole target, cut out by the zero ideal [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Step 4 gives the bound for every limiting ordinary fibre. The scheme limit lemma supplies $i\ge i_0$ for which every ordinary fibre of $g_i$ has dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Tag 0D4K, final application of limits.tex Tag 05M5 (lemma-limit-dimension)

proof.text: For this $i$, take any geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_i$ with image $t_i$. Put $V=(U_i)_{t_i}$ and $W=(U_i)_\Omega$; these are fibres of the stage-$i$ chart, not of the limiting chart $U$. The pullback $W\to (X_i)_\Omega$ of $p_i$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $W=V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t_i)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The scheme $V$ is affine and of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Writing $V=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] makes $B_i$ a finite-type $\kappa(t_i)$-algebra, and the affine fibre-product formula identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_{\kappa(t_i)}\Omega)$. Swapping tensor factors by $b\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes b$ and applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] give $\dim W=\dim V\le d$. The diagonal test calculation in step 3 also proves that $(X_i)_\Omega$ is quasi-separated over $\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-atlas-dimension] with $k=\Omega$, $Y=(X_i)_\Omega$ and its surjective etale atlas $W$. This gives $\dim |(X_i)_\Omega|=\dim W\le d$. This works for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(t_i)$ and requires no equidimensionality.

source.place: Tag 0D4K, return from the scheme chart to the algebraic space; the same Tags 0A4J, 0A4H and 00P3 as in step 4

proof.text: For every $j\ge i$, the map $f_j$ is the base change of $f_i$ along $T_j\to T_i$: by the universal property of algebraic-space fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], pasted as in [def-pc-fibre-product], $X_j=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_j=(X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i)\times_{T_i}T_j=X_i\times_{T_i}T_j$. Apply the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-relative-dimension-base-change] to $f_i$, which is quasi-separated and locally of finite type by step 3: step 6 proves $P_d(f_i)$ (the condition of that node that every geometric fibre has topological Krull dimension at most $d$), i.e. the bound for the geometric fibre over every map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_i$ with $\Omega$ any algebraically closed field, not only a chosen algebraic closure of a residue field. The clause gives $P_d(X_i\times_{T_i}T_j\to T_j)$, so every geometric fibre of $f_j$, over every algebraically closed $\Omega$, has dimension at most $d$. Empty fibres are allowed in $P_d$ (dimension $-\infty$), so no nonemptiness or equidimensionality assumption has entered the argument.
